records.source: וַתִּתְפַּלֵּ֤ל חַנָּה֙ וַתֹּאמַ֔ר עָלַ֤ץ לִבִּי֙ בַּֽיהוָ֔ה רָ֥מָה קַרְנִ֖י בַּֽיהוָ֑ה רָ֤חַב פִּי֙ עַל־א֣וֹיְבַ֔י כִּ֥י שָׂמַ֖חְתִּי בִּישׁוּעָתֶֽךָ׃
records.gloss: And prayed Hannah and said, exults my heart in Yahweh; is lifted high my horn in Yahweh; is wide my mouth over my enemies, for I rejoice in your salvation.
pieces: Then Hannah prayed, and she said: \q "My heart is glad in {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}; \q in {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} my horn is raised high. \q I boast loudly over my enemies, \q because I rejoice in {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} salvation.

L.1: And Hannah prayed and said, \q "My heart exults in {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}; \q my horn is lifted high in {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. \q My mouth is wide over my enemies, \q for I rejoice in {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} salvation.

R.1: Then Hannah prayed: \q "My heart is full of joy because of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. \q {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} has made me strong. \q Now I can laugh at my enemies, \q because I rejoice that {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} have saved me.

decisions.choice: prayed: Hannah's song is called a prayer
decisions.reason: The verb is the one used for Hannah's pleading in 1:10-12 and 1:26-27. Prayer includes praise as well as request: the woman who prayed in tears now prays in thanks. Verses 1-10 are one poem, a song of praise.

decisions.choice: my horn is lifted high: my strength and honor are restored
decisions.reason: The horn of a wild ox stands for its strength and pride (Deuteronomy 33:17; Psalm 92:11). A lifted horn is a picture of someone raised from shame to dignity. Hannah had been mocked for having no children (1:6-7). The poem ends with the same picture for the king (verse 10).

decisions.choice: my mouth is wide over my enemies: I can speak out, even laugh, against those who mocked me
decisions.reason: An open mouth is a picture of boasting or mocking (Psalm 35:21; Isaiah 57:4). Hannah, silenced by her rival's taunts, can now answer them. The enemies are left unnamed, so the song speaks for anyone God has rescued.

decisions.choice: your salvation: the rescue God has given
decisions.reason: The noun means deliverance, help that saves someone from a trouble they cannot escape. Here it is the gift of a son after years of barrenness; the song widens it to God's rescue of the poor and his people (verses 8-10).

decisions.choice: Mary's song in Luke 1:46-55 echoes Hannah's song
decisions.reason: Mary, another woman given a son by God, begins as Hannah does, rejoicing in God her Savior (Luke 1:46-47). Her song takes up Hannah's themes: God lifts the lowly, brings down the proud, fills the hungry and sends the rich away empty (verses 4-8; Luke 1:51-53), and raises a horn of salvation for his anointed king (verse 10; Luke 1:69).

decisions.choice: I boast loudly over (Balanced); I can laugh at (Readable)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the picture of the open mouth. Balanced says what it means, and Readable puts it in everyday words.

decisions.choice: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} has made me strong (Readable)
decisions.reason: Literal and Balanced keep the horn, which returns in verse 10. Readable states the sense and names the LORD as the one who raised her, as the parallel line implies.

decisions.choice: a double quotation mark opens here and closes at the end of verse 10
decisions.reason: The whole poem is Hannah's prayer, so it is set as one quotation. The first line, the narrator's introduction, stands as its own line before the poem begins.

records.heading: Hannah sings to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}

records.source: אֵין־קָד֥וֹשׁ כַּיהוָ֖ה כִּ֣י אֵ֣ין בִּלְתֶּ֑ךָ וְאֵ֥ין צ֖וּר כֵּאלֹהֵֽינוּ׃
records.gloss: There is none holy like Yahweh, for there is none besides you; and there is no rock like our God.
pieces: No one is holy like {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}; \q indeed, there is none but {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}, \q and no rock is like our God.

L.2: There is none holy like {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, \q for there is none besides {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}; \q and there is no rock like our God.

R.2: No one is holy like {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. \q There is no one but {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}. \q No rock keeps us as safe as our God.

decisions.choice: holy: set apart, unlike anyone or anything else
decisions.reason: Holiness is God's otherness: he is in a class of his own (Exodus 15:11). The verse says it three ways: no one is holy like him, there is no one besides him, no rock is like him.

decisions.choice: besides you: the song turns to speak to God directly
decisions.reason: For one line Hannah addresses God ("you"), then speaks about him again ("our God"). Such shifts are common in Hebrew praise (Psalm 23:4-5).

decisions.choice: rock: God as a sure place of safety
decisions.reason: A rock is a high, firm place where someone can find shelter from attack. Scripture often calls God a rock (Deuteronomy 32:4, 31; 2 Samuel 22:2-3, 32; Psalm 18:3).

decisions.choice: No rock keeps us as safe as our God (Readable)
decisions.reason: Readable says what the picture of the rock means: protection and safety.

records.source: אַל־תַּרְבּ֤וּ תְדַבְּרוּ֙ גְּבֹהָ֣ה גְבֹהָ֔ה יֵצֵ֥א עָתָ֖ק מִפִּיכֶ֑ם כִּ֣י אֵ֤ל דֵּעוֹת֙ יְהוָ֔ה וְל֥וֹ נִתְכְּנ֖וּ עֲלִלֽוֹת׃
records.gloss: Do not multiply, you speak proud, proud; [let not] go out arrogance from your mouth; for a God of knowledge [is] Yahweh, and by him are weighed deeds.
pieces: Do not keep talking so proudly, \q or let arrogant words leave your lips, \q for {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} is a God who knows all things, \q and by {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} every action is weighed.

L.3: Do not keep on speaking proudly, so proudly; \q [let not] arrogance come out of your mouth; \q for {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} [is] a God of knowledge, \q and by {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} deeds are weighed.

R.3: Stop all your proud talk! \q Do not say such arrogant things! \q {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} is a God who knows everything, \q and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} judges everything people do.

decisions.choice: do not keep talking proudly, so proudly: a warning to the arrogant
decisions.reason: The commands are plural, spoken to the proud in general. The word "proud" is repeated for emphasis. Behind it stands Hannah's rival, who taunted her year after year (1:6-7), but the song does not name her.

decisions.choice: and by him deeds are weighed, as the scribes' reading has it
alternatives: and actions are not weighed
are not actions weighed?
decisions.reason: The reading the scribes marked (qere) is lo, "by him": God weighs what people do. The written consonants (ketiv) have the word that sounds the same but means "not", which would give "and deeds are not weighed" or, as a question, "are deeds not weighed?" Both say that God judges, but the marked reading says it plainly.

decisions.choice: a God of knowledge: a God who knows fully
decisions.reason: The noun is plural, which stresses how complete his knowledge is. Nothing that the proud say or do escapes him.

decisions.choice: weighed: tested and judged
decisions.reason: God is pictured as weighing deeds on scales to find their true worth (Proverbs 16:2; 21:2; 24:12).

decisions.choice: a God who knows all things (Balanced); a God who knows everything (Readable)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what "God of knowledge" means.

records.source: קֶ֥שֶׁת גִּבֹּרִ֖ים חַתִּ֑ים וְנִכְשָׁלִ֖ים אָ֥זְרוּ חָֽיִל׃
records.gloss: [The] bow of mighty [ones] [are] shattered, and stumbling [ones] gird on strength.
pieces: The bows of the mighty are broken, \q while those who stumbled are armed with strength.

L.4: [The] bow of [the] mighty [are] shattered, \q and [those who] stumble gird on strength.

R.4: The bows of strong soldiers are broken, \q but people who were weak are made strong.

decisions.choice: God turns things upside down: the strong are broken and the weak made strong
decisions.reason: Verses 4-8 list reversals of human fortune. The poem does not name who acts in verses 4-5, but verses 6-8 say it is the LORD. Mary's song takes up the theme (Luke 1:51-53).

decisions.choice: the bow of the mighty are shattered: the warriors are broken along with their weapons
decisions.reason: The verb "shattered" is plural and agrees with "the mighty" rather than with "bow", so the line speaks of the soldiers themselves as well as their bows.

decisions.choice: gird on strength: are made strong, ready to act
decisions.reason: A belt was tightened around the waist before work or battle. To be girded with strength is to be equipped for action (2 Samuel 22:40; Psalm 18:33).

decisions.choice: are armed with strength (Balanced); are made strong (Readable)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps "gird on". Balanced uses a natural picture of being equipped; Readable states the sense.

records.source: שְׂבֵעִ֤ים בַּלֶּ֨חֶם֙ נִשְׂכָּ֔רוּ וּרְעֵבִ֖ים חָדֵ֑לּוּ עַד־עֲקָרָה֙ יָלְדָ֣ה שִׁבְעָ֔ה וְרַבַּ֥ת בָּנִ֖ים אֻמְלָֽלָה׃
records.gloss: [The] full for bread hire themselves out, and [the] hungry cease; until barren bears seven, and many of sons languishes.
pieces: Those who were full hire themselves out for bread, \q but the hungry hunger no more. \q The childless woman gives birth to seven, \q but the mother of many sons pines away.

L.5: [The] full hire themselves out for bread, \q and [the] hungry cease [to hunger]; \q even [the] barren bears seven, \q and [she who has] many sons wastes away.

R.5: People who had plenty to eat now work for food, \q but hungry people now have enough. \q The woman who could not have children has seven, \q but the woman with many sons becomes weak and sad.

decisions.choice: the hungry cease: they hunger no more
alternatives: the hungry grow fat
the hungry rest from their labor
decisions.reason: The verb usually means "stop" or "cease", and the sense is that they stop being hungry. Some take it from a rare word meaning "grow fat", which gives the same picture: the hungry now have plenty.

decisions.choice: until, even: the line moves to the most striking reversal of all
alternatives: the hungry hunger no more forever
decisions.reason: The small word usually means "until" or "up to". Here it introduces the next line: it goes as far as this, that the barren woman bears seven. Others join it to the line before and read a similar word meaning "forever": "the hungry cease from hunger forever".

decisions.choice: seven: a full, complete family
decisions.reason: Seven is the number of completeness (Ruth 4:15, "better to you than seven sons"). Hannah later bore five more children (2:21), not seven; the number is a picture, not a count. The mother of many sons recalls her rival Peninnah (1:2).

decisions.choice: the full and the hungry change places
decisions.reason: Mary sings the same: "he has filled the hungry with good things, and the rich he has sent away with nothing" (Luke 1:53; compare Psalm 107:9).

decisions.choice: hunger no more (Balanced); now have enough (Readable)
decisions.reason: Literal supplies "to hunger" in brackets. Balanced and Readable say plainly what the hungry stop doing.

records.source: יְהוָ֖ה מֵמִ֣ית וּמְחַיֶּ֑ה מוֹרִ֥יד שְׁא֖וֹל וַיָּֽעַל׃
records.gloss: Yahweh kills and makes alive; brings down [to] Sheol and brings up.
pieces: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} brings death and gives life; \q {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} sends down to Sheol and brings up again.

L.6: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} kills and makes alive; \q {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} brings down [to] Sheol and brings up.

R.6: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} causes death and gives life. \q He sends people down to the grave, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} brings them back up.

decisions.choice: the LORD kills and makes alive: he alone rules over life and death
decisions.reason: The same words appear in the Song of Moses: "I put to death and I make alive" (Deuteronomy 32:39). In Hannah's life it means that the LORD who closed her womb (1:5-6) has given her a child.

decisions.choice: Sheol: the place of the dead
decisions.reason: Sheol is the realm of the dead, below the earth. To bring someone down to it is to bring death; to bring someone up from it may mean rescuing a person from the brink of death (Psalm 30:4) or giving life back to the dead. The line keeps both open.

decisions.choice: the grave (Readable)
decisions.reason: Literal and Balanced keep "Sheol". Readable says "the grave", the plain sense for new readers.

records.source: יְהוָ֖ה מוֹרִ֣ישׁ וּמַעֲשִׁ֑יר מַשְׁפִּ֖יל אַף־מְרוֹמֵֽם׃
records.gloss: Yahweh makes poor and makes rich; brings low, also lifts high.
pieces: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} makes some poor and others rich; \q {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} humbles, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} also exalts.

L.7: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} makes poor and makes rich; \q {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} brings low, yes, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} lifts high.

R.7: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} makes some people poor and others rich. \q He brings some down and lifts others up.

decisions.choice: makes poor, makes rich, brings low, lifts high: what the LORD does again and again
decisions.reason: The verbs are participles, describing God's ongoing way of acting rather than one event. The pairs of opposites say that every change of fortune is in his hands (Psalm 75:8).

decisions.choice: brings low and lifts high
decisions.reason: Mary sings, "He has pulled the mighty down from their thrones and raised up the lowly" (Luke 1:52).

decisions.choice: some ... others (Balanced, Readable)
decisions.reason: Hebrew does not name the objects. Balanced and Readable supply "some" and "others" so the English does not sound as if the same people are made both poor and rich at once.

records.source: מֵקִ֨ים מֵעָפָ֜ר דָּ֗ל מֵֽאַשְׁפֹּת֙ יָרִ֣ים אֶבְי֔וֹן לְהוֹשִׁיב֙ עִם־נְדִיבִ֔ים וְכִסֵּ֥א כָב֖וֹד יַנְחִלֵ֑ם כִּ֤י לַֽיהוָה֙ מְצֻ֣קֵי אֶ֔רֶץ וַיָּ֥שֶׁת עֲלֵיהֶ֖ם תֵּבֵֽל׃
records.gloss: raising from dust [the] poor, from [the] ash heap he lifts [the] needy, to make sit with nobles, and a throne of honor he makes them inherit; for to Yahweh [belong the] pillars of [the] earth, and he set on them [the] world.
pieces: He lifts the poor up out of the dust \q and raises those in need from the ash heap, \q to seat them with nobles \q and give them a throne of honor as their own. \q For the pillars of the earth belong to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}; \q on them {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} has set the world.

L.8: He raises [the] poor from [the] dust; \q from [the] ash heap {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} lifts [the] needy, \q to seat [them] with nobles, \q and a throne of honor {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} gives them to inherit. \q For to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} [belong the] pillars of [the] earth, \q and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} has set the world on them.

R.8: He lifts poor people out of the dirt. \q He raises needy people from the garbage heap. \q He seats them with princes and gives them places of honor. \q The foundations of the earth belong to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, \q and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} has set the world on them.

decisions.choice: the same words as Psalm 113:7-8
decisions.reason: The first two lines and the start of the third are almost word for word in Psalm 113:7-8, where they are followed, as here, by the barren woman who becomes a glad mother (Psalm 113:9). The wording here follows that psalm. Psalm 113:8 adds "with the nobles of his people"; this verse goes on to the throne of honor instead.

decisions.choice: the ash heap: the town's refuse heap, where the outcast and destitute sat
decisions.reason: Ash and refuse were dumped outside the town. The very poor, the sick and the shamed sat and begged there. To be lifted from it to sit among nobles is the greatest possible change of rank.

decisions.choice: a throne of honor he makes them inherit: a place of honor given to them to keep
decisions.reason: The verb means to give as an inheritance, a lasting possession. The seat is a seat of rank among the nobles.

decisions.choice: the pillars of the earth: the foundations on which the world stands
decisions.reason: The poem pictures the earth resting on pillars that God himself set in place (Psalm 75:4; 104:5). Because he made and holds up the world, he has the right to reorder it as the verse describes.

decisions.choice: ash heap (Balanced); garbage heap (Readable)
decisions.reason: Readable uses an everyday word for the place where refuse was dumped.

decisions.choice: the foundations of the earth (Readable)
decisions.reason: Readable says "foundations" for the pillars on which the earth was pictured as resting.

records.source: רַגְלֵ֤י חֲסִידָיו֙ יִשְׁמֹ֔ר וּרְשָׁעִ֖ים בַּחֹ֣שֶׁךְ יִדָּ֑מּוּ כִּֽי־לֹ֥א בְכֹ֖חַ יִגְבַּר־אִֽישׁ׃
records.gloss: [The] feet of his faithful [ones] he guards, and [the] wicked in darkness are silenced; for not by strength prevails a man.
pieces: He guards the steps of {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} faithful ones, \q but the wicked are silenced in darkness, \q for no one wins by strength.

L.9: [The] feet of {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} faithful ones {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} guards, \q but [the] wicked are silenced in darkness; \q for not by strength does [anyone] prevail.

R.9: He keeps {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} faithful people from stumbling, \q but wicked people will be silenced in the dark. \q No one wins just by being strong.

decisions.choice: his faithful ones, as the scribes' reading has it
alternatives: his faithful one
decisions.reason: The written consonants (ketiv) read "his faithful one" (singular); the reading the scribes marked (qere) is plural. The singular would speak of each faithful person in turn. The meaning is the same.

decisions.choice: he guards the feet: he keeps them from stumbling or falling
decisions.reason: Feet stand for a person's path through life. God keeps them from slipping into harm (Psalm 116:8; 121:3).

decisions.choice: faithful ones: those who are loyal to God
decisions.reason: The word comes from chesed, steadfast love. It names those who keep faith with God and his covenant.

decisions.choice: silenced in darkness: brought to silence in death or disaster
decisions.reason: The verb means "be silent" and is also used for being cut off or destroyed (Jeremiah 8:14; Psalm 31:18). The wicked who boasted (verse 3) are silenced; darkness is the darkness of ruin and death.

decisions.choice: a man: anyone
decisions.reason: The noun "man" is used here for any human being. No one wins by strength alone; victory comes from the LORD (verse 10; Psalm 33:16-17).

records.source: יְהוָ֞ה יֵחַ֣תּוּ מְרִיבָ֗יו עָלָיו֙ בַּשָּׁמַ֣יִם יַרְעֵ֔ם יְהוָ֖ה יָדִ֣ין אַפְסֵי־אָ֑רֶץ וְיִתֶּן־עֹ֣ז לְמַלְכּ֔וֹ וְיָרֵ֖ם קֶ֥רֶן מְשִׁיחֽוֹ׃פ
records.gloss: Yahweh, are shattered those contending with him; against him in the heavens he thunders; Yahweh judges [the] ends of [the] earth, and gives strength to his king, and lifts high [the] horn of his anointed.
pieces: Those who oppose {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} will be shattered; \q {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will thunder against them from heaven. \q {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} will judge the ends of the earth; \q {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will grant strength to {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} king \q and raise high the horn of {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} anointed."

L.10: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}}, those who contend with {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} will be shattered; \q against them in the heavens {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will thunder. \q {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} will judge the ends of the earth; \q {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will give strength to {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} king \q and lift high the horn of {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} anointed."

R.10: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} will break to pieces everyone who fights against {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}. \q He will thunder against them from the sky. \q {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} will judge the whole earth, to its farthest edges. \q He will make {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} king strong and give great power to the king {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} has anointed."

decisions.choice: will be shattered, will thunder, will judge, will give, will lift high: what the LORD will do
alternatives: those who oppose the LORD are shattered ...
may he give strength to his king
decisions.reason: The verbs are imperfect and look ahead. Hannah's song ends with what God will do, not only with what he has done. They could also be read as what God always does, or as a prayer ("may he give strength to his king").

decisions.choice: those who contend with him, as the scribes' reading has it
alternatives: the one who contends with him
decisions.reason: The written consonants (ketiv) read "the one who contends with him" (singular); the reading the scribes marked (qere) is plural. The pronoun in "against him" is singular in the Hebrew: the LORD thunders against each opponent. The ancient Greek translation adds a long passage here, close to Jeremiah 9:22-23 ("let not the wise boast in his wisdom ... but let the one who boasts boast in this, that he understands and knows the LORD"). The Hebrew text, which governs, does not have it. Reviewers should check this note against the textual evidence.

decisions.choice: his king, his anointed: the king God will appoint and anoint
alternatives: his Messiah
decisions.reason: This is the first time Scripture calls a king the LORD's anointed. Earlier the word was used of the anointed priest (Leviticus 4:3, 5, 16). Israel had no king yet (Judges 21:25); the song looks ahead to the kings Samuel will anoint (10:1; 16:13). The Hebrew word is mashiach, from which "Messiah" comes, and later hope looked for a final anointed king. Luke 1:69 echoes this line: God "has raised up a horn of salvation for us in the house of David."

decisions.choice: lift high the horn: give strength and honor
decisions.reason: The song ends with the picture it began with (verse 1). What God did for Hannah he will do for his king.

decisions.choice: thunder from heaven: God as a warrior against his enemies
decisions.reason: God's voice is heard in thunder as he fights for his people (7:10; 2 Samuel 22:14; Psalm 18:14). In 7:10 he thunders against the Philistines in Samuel's day.

decisions.choice: Those who oppose the LORD will be shattered (Balanced); The LORD will break to pieces everyone who fights against him (Readable)
decisions.reason: Hebrew puts "the LORD" first for emphasis and then says what happens to his enemies. Literal keeps that order; Balanced moves the name into the clause; Readable makes the LORD the subject, as the next line does.

decisions.choice: the king he has anointed (Readable)
decisions.reason: Literal and Balanced say "his anointed". Readable says who is meant, as it does for "the LORD's anointed" throughout Samuel. The double quotation mark that opened in verse 1 closes here at every level.

records.source: וַיֵּ֧לֶךְ אֶלְקָנָ֛ה הָרָמָ֖תָה עַל־בֵּית֑וֹ וְהַנַּ֗עַר הָיָ֤ה מְשָׁרֵת֙ אֶת־יְהוָ֔ה אֶת־פְּנֵ֖י עֵלִ֥י הַכֹּהֵֽן׃
records.gloss: And went Elkanah to Ramah to his house; and the boy was serving Yahweh in [the] presence of Eli the priest.
pieces: Then Elkanah went home to Ramah, but the boy stayed and served {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} under Eli the priest.

L.11: And Elkanah went to Ramah, to his house; and the boy was serving {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} in the presence of Eli the priest.

R.11: Then Elkanah went back home to Ramah. But the boy Samuel stayed at Shiloh to serve {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} under Eli the priest.

decisions.choice: Elkanah went home: the family returns without the boy
decisions.reason: Only Elkanah is named, as head of the family, but Hannah goes with him: verse 19 has her coming up each year with her husband. Samuel stays behind at Shiloh, as Hannah had promised (1:22, 28).

decisions.choice: serving: ministering at the sanctuary
decisions.reason: The verb is used for the duties of priests and Levites in worship (Numbers 3:6; Deuteronomy 10:8). It is a word of honored service, and it returns in verse 18.

decisions.choice: in the presence of Eli: under Eli's oversight
decisions.reason: The boy serves the LORD, but under the care and direction of the old priest (3:1).

decisions.choice: stayed (Balanced, Readable); the boy Samuel, at Shiloh (Readable)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what the contrast implies: Elkanah went home, but the boy stayed. Readable names Samuel and the place, which the context makes clear (1:24).

records.heading: Eli's sons treat the offerings with contempt

records.source: וּבְנֵ֥י עֵלִ֖י בְּנֵ֣י בְלִיָּ֑עַל לֹ֥א יָדְע֖וּ אֶת־יְהוָֽה׃
records.gloss: And [the] sons of Eli [were] sons of worthlessness; not they knew Yahweh.
pieces: Now Eli's sons were worthless men; they did not know {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

L.12: And the sons of Eli [were] sons of worthlessness; they did not know {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

R.12: Eli's sons were wicked men. They had no respect for {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

decisions.choice: sons of worthlessness: good-for-nothing, wicked men
decisions.reason: The Hebrew calls people "sons of" a quality they show. The word beliyya'al means worthlessness or wickedness (Deuteronomy 13:14; Judges 19:22). Hannah had begged Eli not to count her "a daughter of worthlessness" (1:16); the irony is that his own sons are the worthless ones.

decisions.choice: they did not know the LORD: they did not acknowledge or honor him
decisions.reason: To know the LORD is more than to know about him: it is to recognize his claim and live by it (Judges 2:10; Jeremiah 22:16). These are priests who serve at his altar, yet they do not know him.

decisions.choice: Eli's sons: Hophni and Phinehas, priests at Shiloh
decisions.reason: They were named in 1:3, and their names return in verse 34.

decisions.choice: they had no respect for (Readable)
decisions.reason: Readable says what "not knowing" the LORD meant here, as the next verses show.

records.source: וּמִשְׁפַּ֥ט הַכֹּהֲנִ֖ים אֶת־הָעָ֑ם כָּל־אִ֞ישׁ זֹבֵ֣חַ זֶ֗בַח וּבָ֨א נַ֤עַר הַכֹּהֵן֙ כְּבַשֵּׁ֣ל הַבָּשָׂ֔ר וְהַמַּזְלֵ֛ג שְׁלֹ֥שׁ־הַשִּׁנַּ֖יִם בְּיָדֽוֹ׃
records.gloss: And [the] custom of the priests with the people: any man sacrificing a sacrifice, and would come [the] servant of the priest as the meat was boiling, and the fork of three prongs in his hand,
pieces: Now this was the priests' practice with the people: whenever anyone offered a sacrifice, the priest's servant would come while the meat was boiling, carrying a three-pronged fork,

L.13: And the custom of the priests with the people [was this]: whenever any man offered a sacrifice, the priest's servant would come while the meat was boiling, with a fork of three prongs in his hand,

R.13: This is how the priests treated the people. Whenever someone offered a sacrifice, the priest's servant came while the meat was still boiling. He carried a large fork with three prongs.

decisions.choice: the custom of the priests: what they had made their practice
alternatives: the priests' right from the people
decisions.reason: The noun often means a legal right or ruling, and the law did give the priest a share of each peace offering: the breast and the right thigh (Leviticus 7:31-34; compare Deuteronomy 18:3). Here it is the practice Eli's sons had made for themselves, taking more than their share, and taking it before God's portion was burned (verse 15).

decisions.choice: a new sentence begins with "the custom of the priests"
alternatives: they did not know the LORD, nor the priests' rightful share from the people
decisions.reason: The Hebrew verse division starts a new sentence here. The ancient Greek translation joins the words to the end of verse 12: the sons did not know the LORD "or the priests' due from the people". The Hebrew division governs.

decisions.choice: a sacrifice: a peace offering, which the worshiper's family ate
decisions.reason: In this kind of sacrifice the fat was burned on the altar for the LORD, the priest received his set portion, and the rest of the meat was boiled and eaten by the family in a meal at the sanctuary (1:4; Leviticus 7:11-18, 28-34).

decisions.choice: would come, would thrust: something done again and again
decisions.reason: The verb forms describe a habit, what happened every time someone sacrificed, not one occasion.

decisions.choice: whenever any man (Literal); whenever anyone (Balanced); whenever someone (Readable)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew sets the words side by side, "any man sacrificing a sacrifice"; English needs "whenever". Balanced and Readable use words that include any worshiper.

records.source: וְהִכָּ֨ה בַכִּיּ֜וֹר א֣וֹ בַדּ֗וּד א֤וֹ בַקַּלַּ֨חַת֙ א֣וֹ בַפָּר֔וּר כֹּ֚ל אֲשֶׁ֣ר יַעֲלֶ֣ה הַמַּזְלֵ֔ג יִקַּ֥ח הַכֹּהֵ֖ן בּ֑וֹ כָּ֚כָה יַעֲשׂ֣וּ לְכָל־יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל הַבָּאִ֥ים שָׁ֖ם בְּשִׁלֹֽה׃
records.gloss: and he would thrust into the pan or into the kettle or into the cauldron or into the pot; all that brought up the fork would take the priest for himself. Thus they did to all Israel who came there to Shiloh.
pieces: and he would plunge it into the pan or kettle or cauldron or pot. Whatever the fork brought up, the priest took for himself. This is how they treated all the Israelites who came there to Shiloh.

L.14: and he would thrust [it] into the pan, or into the kettle, or into the cauldron, or into the pot; all that the fork brought up the priest would take for himself. Thus they did to all Israel who came there, to Shiloh.

R.14: He would stab the fork into the cooking pot, and the priest kept for himself whatever meat came up on it. They did this to every Israelite who came to Shiloh.

decisions.choice: pan, kettle, cauldron, pot: cooking pots of different kinds
decisions.reason: The four words name different vessels for boiling meat. Their exact shapes are not known. Listed together, they mean whatever pot the meat was in.

decisions.choice: whatever the fork brought up the priest took: a share left to chance and greed
decisions.reason: The law named the parts that belonged to the priest (Leviticus 7:31-34). Here the priest takes whatever the fork happens to bring up, from the worshipers' own share of the meal.

decisions.choice: the priest: whichever priest sent the servant
decisions.reason: The singular speaks of each priest in turn; from verses 12 and 17 it is Eli's sons who did this.

decisions.choice: the cooking pot (Readable)
decisions.reason: Readable gives one word for the four kinds of pot, since the point is that any pot would do.

records.source: גַּם֮ בְּטֶרֶם֮ יַקְטִר֣וּן אֶת־הַחֵלֶב֒ וּבָ֣א׀נַ֣עַר הַכֹּהֵ֗ן וְאָמַר֙ לָאִ֣ישׁ הַזֹּבֵ֔חַ תְּנָ֣ה בָשָׂ֔ר לִצְל֖וֹת לַכֹּהֵ֑ן וְלֹֽא־יִקַּ֧ח מִמְּךָ֛ בָּשָׂ֥ר מְבֻשָּׁ֖ל כִּ֥י אִם־חָֽי׃
records.gloss: Also before they made smoke [of] the fat, and would come [the] servant of the priest and say to the man sacrificing, give meat to roast for the priest; and not he will take from you meat boiled, but only raw.
pieces: Worse still, before the fat had even been turned into smoke, the priest's servant would come and tell the man offering the sacrifice, "Hand over some meat for the priest to roast. He will not accept boiled meat from you, only raw."

L.15: Even before they turned the fat into smoke, the priest's servant would come and say to the man who was sacrificing, "Give meat to roast for the priest; he will not take boiled meat from you, only raw."

R.15: Even before the fat was burned on the altar, the priest's servant would come. He would say to the man offering the sacrifice, "Give the priest some meat to roast. He will not take boiled meat from you. He wants it raw."

decisions.choice: before the fat was burned: they took their share before God received his
decisions.reason: The fat of every peace offering belonged to the LORD and had to be burned on the altar first (Leviticus 3:16-17; 7:30-31). Taking meat before that put the priests ahead of God.

decisions.choice: roast, not boiled: the priest wanted the better meat, chosen raw
decisions.reason: Roasting was the finer way to cook meat. Taking it raw also let the priest pick the best pieces before anything was cooked.

decisions.choice: they turned the fat into smoke: the people offering, or anyone burning it
decisions.reason: The subject "they" is general: before anyone had burned the fat.

decisions.choice: turned the fat into smoke (Literal, Balanced); was burned on the altar (Readable)
decisions.reason: The verb means to make something go up in smoke, the word used for burning offerings on the altar in Leviticus. Readable says "burned on the altar".

records.source: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר אֵלָ֜יו הָאִ֗ישׁ קַטֵּ֨ר יַקְטִיר֤וּן כַּיּוֹם֙ הַחֵ֔לֶב וְקַ֨ח־לְךָ֔ כַּאֲשֶׁ֥ר תְּאַוֶּ֖ה נַפְשֶׁ֑ךָ וְאָמַ֥ר׀לֹא֙ כִּ֚י עַתָּ֣ה תִתֵּ֔ן וְאִם־לֹ֖א לָקַ֥חְתִּי בְחָזְקָֽה׃
records.gloss: And would say to him the man, let them surely make smoke as the day [of] the fat, and take for yourself as desires your appetite; and he would say, no, for now you will give, and if not, I will take by force.
pieces: If the man answered, "Let the fat be turned into smoke first, and then take whatever you like," the servant would say, "No, hand it over now. If you do not, I will take it by force."

L.16: And [if] the man said to him, "Let them be sure to turn the fat into smoke first, and then take for yourself whatever your appetite desires," he would say, "No! You will give [it] now; and if not, I will take [it] by force."

R.16: The man might say, "First let the fat be burned up, as it should be. Then take as much as you want." But the servant would answer, "No! Give it to me now. If you do not, I will take it by force."

decisions.choice: no, as the scribes' reading has it
alternatives: he would say to him
decisions.reason: The reading the scribes marked (qere) is lo', "no". The written consonants (ketiv) have the word that sounds the same but means "to him": "he would say to him, 'You will give it now.'" The meaning is the same: the servant refuses to wait.

decisions.choice: as the day: first, without delay
decisions.reason: The phrase means "at once" or "first, as is right". The worshiper asks only that God's portion come first, as the law required.

decisions.choice: as your appetite desires: whatever you want
decisions.reason: The noun nefesh here means appetite or desire. The worshiper offers the priest all he wants, once the fat is burned.

decisions.choice: the servant (Balanced, Readable); as it should be (Readable)
decisions.reason: Hebrew says only "he would say". Balanced and Readable name the servant so the reader knows who refuses. Readable adds "as it should be" to show that the worshiper asks only for what the law required.

records.source: וַתְּהִ֨י חַטַּ֧את הַנְּעָרִ֛ים גְּדוֹלָ֥ה מְאֹ֖ד אֶת־פְּנֵ֣י יְהוָ֑ה כִּ֤י נִֽאֲצוּ֙ הָֽאֲנָשִׁ֔ים אֵ֖ת מִנְחַ֥ת יְהוָֽה׃
records.gloss: And was [the] sin of the young men very great in [the] presence of Yahweh, for treated with contempt the men the offering of Yahweh.
pieces: So the sin of these young men was very great in the sight of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, for they treated {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}'s offering with contempt.

L.17: And the sin of the young men was very great before {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, for the men treated the offering of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} with contempt.

R.17: These young men were sinning very greatly against {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. They treated the offerings people brought to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} as if they did not matter.

decisions.choice: the young men: Eli's sons
alternatives: the servants
decisions.reason: The word can mean servants, as it does in verses 13 and 15, but here it points to Eli's sons, whose sin the passage describes (verses 12, 22-25). They are young compared with their father.

decisions.choice: the men treated the offering with contempt: the priests, or the people
alternatives: the people came to treat the LORD's offering with contempt
decisions.reason: "The men" most likely means the same young men, who despised the offering. It could also mean that because of them, the people came to despise the LORD's offering. Either way the guilt lies with the priests.

decisions.choice: the offering of the LORD: every gift brought to God, not only grain
decisions.reason: The noun minchah can name the grain offering (Leviticus 2), but here it means any offering given to the LORD.

decisions.choice: as if they did not matter (Readable)
decisions.reason: Readable explains "treated with contempt" in plain words.

records.source: וּשְׁמוּאֵ֕ל מְשָׁרֵ֖ת אֶת־פְּנֵ֣י יְהוָ֑ה נַ֕עַר חָג֖וּר אֵפ֥וֹד בָּֽד׃
records.gloss: And Samuel [was] serving in [the] presence of Yahweh, a boy girded [with an] ephod of linen.
pieces: Samuel, meanwhile, was serving before {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, a boy wearing a linen ephod.

L.18: But Samuel was serving before {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, a boy girded with a linen ephod.

R.18: But the boy Samuel served {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. He wore a linen ephod, a simple garment that priests wore.

decisions.choice: but Samuel: the story sets the boy against Eli's sons
decisions.reason: The sentence starts with Samuel's name, a contrast with the young men of verse 17. The chapter moves back and forth between Samuel and Eli's sons (verses 11, 18, 21, 26).

decisions.choice: a linen ephod: a simple garment worn by those serving at the sanctuary
decisions.reason: The plain linen ephod was worn by priests (22:18) and by David when he danced before the ark (2 Samuel 6:14). It was different from the high priest's richly made ephod with its breastpiece (Exodus 28:6-14), the ephod Eli's family carried (verse 28).

decisions.choice: a simple garment that priests wore (Readable)
decisions.reason: Readable keeps the word "ephod" and explains it briefly.

records.source: וּמְעִ֤יל קָטֹן֙ תַּעֲשֶׂה־לּ֣וֹ אִמּ֔וֹ וְהַעַלְתָ֥ה ל֖וֹ מִיָּמִ֣ים׀יָמִ֑ימָה בַּֽעֲלוֹתָהּ֙ אֶת־אִישָׁ֔הּ לִזְבֹּ֖חַ אֶת־זֶ֥בַח הַיָּמִֽים׃
records.gloss: And a robe small would make for him his mother, and bring [it] up to him from days to days, in her going up with her husband to sacrifice the sacrifice of the days.
pieces: Each year his mother made him a small robe and brought it to him when she went up with her husband for the yearly sacrifice.

L.19: And his mother would make him a little robe and bring [it] up to him from year to year, when she went up with her husband to offer the yearly sacrifice.

R.19: Every year his mother made him a little robe. She brought it to him when she and her husband came to offer the yearly sacrifice.

decisions.choice: from days to days, the sacrifice of the days: year by year, the yearly sacrifice
decisions.reason: "Days" here means a full round of days, a year, as in 1:3, 21.

decisions.choice: a robe: an outer garment
decisions.reason: The me'il was a sleeveless outer robe. Samuel's robe comes back in his story (15:27; 28:14). His mother's care continues though she has given him to the LORD.

decisions.choice: from year to year (Literal)
decisions.reason: Literal says "year" because "from days to days" would not be understood. The gloss keeps the Hebrew.

records.source: וּבֵרַ֨ךְ עֵלִ֜י אֶת־אֶלְקָנָ֣ה וְאֶת־אִשְׁתּ֗וֹ וְאָמַר֙ יָשֵׂם֩ יְהוָ֨ה לְךָ֥ זֶ֨רַע֙ מִן־הָאִשָּׁ֣ה הַזֹּ֔את תַּ֚חַת הַשְּׁאֵלָ֔ה אֲשֶׁ֥ר שָׁאַ֖ל לַֽיהוָ֑ה וְהָלְכ֖וּ לִמְקֹמֽוֹ׃
records.gloss: And would bless Eli Elkanah and his wife and say, may set Yahweh for you offspring from the woman this in place of the request which he asked for Yahweh. And they would go to his place.
pieces: Eli would bless Elkanah and his wife and say, "May {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} give you children by this woman to take the place of the one she asked for and gave to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}." Then they would go home.

L.20: And Eli would bless Elkanah and his wife and say, "May {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} give you offspring from this woman in place of the one asked for, who was asked for {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}." And they would go to his place.

R.20: Eli would bless Elkanah and his wife. He would say to Elkanah, "May {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} give you more children by this woman. They will take the place of the child she asked for and gave back to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}." Then they would go back home.

decisions.choice: the one asked for: Samuel, asked of God and given to God
decisions.reason: The noun and the verb come from the root sha'al, "ask", which runs through chapter 1: Hannah asked for a son (1:17, 20, 27), and she gave him over to the LORD (1:28, "I have lent him to the LORD"). With "for the LORD", the verb here has the second sense: the one asked for has been dedicated to the LORD.

decisions.choice: who was asked for the LORD: the Hebrew says "he asked"
alternatives: which he lent to the LORD
which you lent to the LORD
decisions.reason: The verb is masculine, "he asked". It may be impersonal ("one asked"), or refer to Elkanah, who agreed to Hannah's vow (1:23). The ancient Greek translation reads "you lent". Hannah is the one who asked and gave (1:27-28), and the sense is the same.

decisions.choice: offspring: children
decisions.reason: The noun means seed, descendants. Eli prays that Hannah will have more children to make up for the son she gave away. Verse 21 tells how the LORD answered.

decisions.choice: to his place: home to Ramah
decisions.reason: "His place" is Elkanah's home as head of the family (verse 11; 1:19).

decisions.choice: she asked for and gave (Balanced); she asked for and gave back (Readable)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable make the asker the subject, as chapter 1 does; Literal keeps the impersonal form. Readable adds that Eli spoke to Elkanah, as "you" in the blessing is singular.

records.source: כִּֽי־פָקַ֤ד יְהוָה֙ אֶת־חַנָּ֔ה וַתַּ֛הַר וַתֵּ֥לֶד שְׁלֹשָֽׁה־בָנִ֖ים וּשְׁתֵּ֣י בָנ֑וֹת וַיִּגְדַּ֛ל הַנַּ֥עַר שְׁמוּאֵ֖ל עִם־יְהוָֽה׃ס
records.gloss: For visited Yahweh Hannah, and she conceived and bore three sons and two daughters. And grew the boy Samuel with Yahweh.
pieces: And {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} came to Hannah's aid: she conceived and bore three sons and two daughters. And all the while the boy Samuel was growing up in the presence of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

L.21: Indeed, {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} visited Hannah, and she conceived and bore three sons and two daughters. And the boy Samuel grew up with {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

R.21: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} was kind to Hannah. She became pregnant and had three more sons and two daughters. And the boy Samuel grew up there, serving {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

decisions.choice: for, indeed: the word introduces what followed Eli's blessing
decisions.reason: The word usually means "for" or "because", but here it introduces the outcome of the blessing: indeed, the LORD answered it. The ancient Greek translation has "and".

decisions.choice: visited: came to help
decisions.reason: When God "visits" someone, he pays attention to them and acts, here in kindness, as when he visited Sarah and she conceived (Genesis 21:1).

decisions.choice: with the LORD: at the sanctuary, in the LORD's presence
decisions.reason: Samuel grew up at the house of the LORD in Shiloh, near the ark (3:3).

decisions.choice: came to Hannah's aid (Balanced); was kind to Hannah (Readable)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps "visited". In English that sounds like a social call, so Balanced and Readable say what it meant.

decisions.choice: three more sons (Readable); there, serving the LORD (Readable)
decisions.reason: Readable adds "more" because these sons were born after Samuel, and says Samuel grew up "there, serving the LORD", which verses 11 and 18 make clear.

records.source: וְעֵלִ֖י זָקֵ֣ן מְאֹ֑ד וְשָׁמַ֗ע אֵת֩ כָּל־אֲשֶׁ֨ר יַעֲשׂ֤וּן בָּנָיו֙ לְכָל־יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל וְאֵ֤ת אֲשֶֽׁר־יִשְׁכְּבוּן֙ אֶת־הַנָּשִׁ֔ים הַצֹּ֣בְא֔וֹת פֶּ֖תַח אֹ֥הֶל מוֹעֵֽד׃
records.gloss: And Eli [was] old very, and he heard all that were doing his sons to all Israel, and how they were lying with the women who served [at the] entrance of [the] tent of meeting.
pieces: Eli was now very old. He kept hearing of all that his sons were doing to all Israel, and that they slept with the women serving at the entrance to the tent of meeting.

L.22: And Eli [was] very old, and he heard all that his sons were doing to all Israel, and how they were lying with the women who served at the entrance of the tent of meeting.

R.22: Eli was now very old. He heard about everything his sons were doing to the people of Israel. He heard that they were sleeping with the women who served at the entrance of the meeting tent.

decisions.choice: the second half of the verse, about the women, is in the Hebrew text
decisions.reason: The words "and how they were lying with the women who served at the entrance of the tent of meeting" are lacking in a Dead Sea Scroll of Samuel and in the main manuscripts of the ancient Greek translation. The Hebrew text, which governs, has them. Reviewers should check this note against the textual evidence.

decisions.choice: the women who served at the entrance: women with some duty at the sanctuary
decisions.reason: The same phrase is used in Exodus 38:8 for women whose bronze mirrors were made into the basin. What their service was is not known. The sons' sin is worse because it was done at the place of worship.

decisions.choice: he heard: kept hearing
decisions.reason: The verb form suggests that reports kept reaching him, as verses 23-24 say.

decisions.choice: the meeting tent (Readable)
decisions.reason: Readable says "the meeting tent" for the tent of meeting, as Exodus and Numbers do.

records.heading: Eli warns his sons

records.source: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר לָהֶ֔ם לָ֥מָּה תַעֲשׂ֖וּן כַּדְּבָרִ֣ים הָאֵ֑לֶּה אֲשֶׁ֨ר אָנֹכִ֤י שֹׁמֵ֨עַ֙ אֶת־דִּבְרֵיכֶ֣ם רָעִ֔ים מֵאֵ֖ת כָּל־הָעָ֥ם אֵֽלֶּה׃
records.gloss: And he said to them, why are you doing according to things these, that I am hearing your evil dealings from all the people these?
pieces: He said to them, "Why are you doing these things? I keep hearing from all the people about the evil you are doing.

L.23: And he said to them, "Why are you doing things like these? For I hear of your evil dealings from all these people.

R.23: He said to them, "Why are you doing these things? I hear about your evil ways from everyone.

decisions.choice: why are you doing such things, that I hear of: one question, which L and B divide
decisions.reason: Hebrew runs on: "why do you do such things as I am hearing, your evil deeds, from all these people?" The question is a rebuke, not a request for information.

decisions.choice: all these people: the worshipers who come to Shiloh
decisions.reason: "These" points to the people around him, those who bring their sacrifices and complain of the sons' treatment.

decisions.choice: a double quotation mark opens here and closes in verse 25
decisions.reason: Eli's words to his sons run through verse 25.

records.source: אַ֖ל בָּנָ֑י כִּ֠י לֽוֹא־טוֹבָ֤ה הַשְּׁמֻעָה֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר אָנֹכִ֣י שֹׁמֵ֔עַ מַעֲבִרִ֖ים עַם־יְהוָֽה׃
records.gloss: No, my sons, for not good [is] the report which I am hearing; are spreading [it the] people of Yahweh.
pieces: No, my sons! The report I hear spreading among {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}'s people is not good.

L.24: No, my sons! For the report that I am hearing is not good: the people of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} are spreading [it].

R.24: Stop this, my sons! I hear {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}'s people saying bad things about you.

decisions.choice: the LORD's people are spreading it
alternatives: you are making the LORD's people transgress
decisions.reason: The verb means to make something pass along, here a report passed from person to person. It can also mean "cause to transgress", which would give "you are making the LORD's people sin": their conduct leads the people astray. The verb is plural, and the people are the nearest subject.

decisions.choice: No, my sons: a strong plea to stop
decisions.reason: Eli's "no" breaks off the question with a plea. He rebukes them but does not stop them, which the LORD holds against him (3:13).

decisions.choice: Stop this (Readable)
decisions.reason: Readable says what Eli's "No!" means.

records.source: אִם־יֶחֱטָ֨א אִ֤ישׁ לְאִישׁ֙ וּפִֽלְל֣וֹ אֱלֹהִ֔ים וְאִ֤ם לַֽיהוָה֙ יֶֽחֱטָא־אִ֔ישׁ מִ֖י יִתְפַּלֶּל־ל֑וֹ וְלֹ֤א יִשְׁמְעוּ֙ לְק֣וֹל אֲבִיהֶ֔ם כִּֽי־חָפֵ֥ץ יְהוָ֖ה לַהֲמִיתָֽם׃
records.gloss: If sins a man against a man, will mediate for him God; but if against Yahweh sins a man, who will intercede for him? And not they listened to [the] voice of their father, for desired Yahweh to put them to death.
pieces: If one person sins against another, God can settle the matter; but if someone sins against {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, who can plead for that person?" But they would not listen to their father, because {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} had decided to put them to death.

L.25: If {{gender:a person|a man}} sins against another, God will mediate for {{gender:that person|him}}; but if {{gender:a person|a man}} sins against {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, who will intercede for {{gender:that person|him}}?" But they would not listen to the voice of their father, for {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} desired to put them to death.

R.25: If one person sins against another, God can settle the matter between them. But if someone sins against {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, who can speak up for them?" Still Eli's sons would not listen to their father, because {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} had already decided to put them to death.

decisions.choice: God will mediate: God, or judges acting for God
alternatives: the judges will mediate for him
decisions.reason: The word is the ordinary word for God. In some laws it may refer to judges who decide cases before God (Exodus 21:6; 22:7-8), which would give "the judges will settle it". Either way, a wrong done to a person can be settled by a higher authority; a sin against the LORD himself leaves no one above to appeal to.

decisions.choice: mediate, intercede: two forms of one verb
decisions.reason: The first form means to arbitrate or settle a case; the second, the word for praying, means to plead on someone's behalf. It is the verb used for Hannah's prayer (1:10; 2:1).

decisions.choice: the LORD desired to put them to death: their refusal was itself part of his judgment
decisions.reason: Their deafness to their father is not the reason for God's judgment but its sign: their guilt was already settled (verse 34; 3:13-14). Scripture speaks the same way of Pharaoh's hardened heart (Exodus 10:1, 20).

decisions.choice: a person, that person (Literal); one person, someone (Balanced, Readable)
decisions.reason: The saying applies to anyone, man or woman. Literal gives the traditional "a man ... him" as the alternative; Balanced and Readable use words that are already inclusive. The quotation that opened in verse 23 closes here.

records.source: וְהַנַּ֣עַר שְׁמוּאֵ֔ל הֹלֵ֥ךְ וְגָדֵ֖ל וָט֑וֹב גַּ֚ם עִם־יְהוָ֔ה וְגַ֖ם עִם־אֲנָשִֽׁים׃ס
records.gloss: And the boy Samuel [was] going and growing and good both with Yahweh and also with men.
pieces: Meanwhile the boy Samuel went on growing up, and both {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} and the people were pleased with him.

L.26: And the boy Samuel kept growing, and [was] good both with {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} and with people.

R.26: But the boy Samuel kept growing, and {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} and the people liked him more and more.

decisions.choice: was going and growing and good: grew steadily in size and in favor
decisions.reason: "Going" with another verb means "more and more". "Good with" someone means pleasing to them, in favor with them.

decisions.choice: in favor with the LORD and with people
decisions.reason: Luke uses almost the same words of the boy Jesus: he grew "in favor with God and people" (Luke 2:52; compare 2:40).

decisions.choice: and the boy Samuel: again set against Eli's sons
decisions.reason: Each picture of the sons' evil is followed by one of Samuel growing (verses 11, 18, 21).

decisions.choice: were pleased with him (Balanced); liked him more and more (Readable)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what "good with" means. Readable keeps the sense of growing favor in "more and more".

records.source: וַיָּבֹ֥א אִישׁ־אֱלֹהִ֖ים אֶל־עֵלִ֑י וַיֹּ֣אמֶר אֵלָ֗יו כֹּ֚ה אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֔ה הֲנִגְלֹ֤ה נִגְלֵ֨יתִי֙ אֶל־בֵּ֣ית אָבִ֔יךָ בִּֽהְיוֹתָ֥ם בְּמִצְרַ֖יִם לְבֵ֥ית פַּרְעֹֽה׃
records.gloss: And came a man of God to Eli and said to him, thus says Yahweh: did I indeed reveal myself to [the] house of your father in their being in Egypt, to [the] house of Pharaoh?
pieces: A man of God came to Eli and said to him, "{{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} says this: 'Did I not plainly reveal {{deity_pronoun:myself|Myself}} to your ancestor's family when they were in Egypt, subject to Pharaoh's house?

L.27: And a man of God came to Eli and said to him, "Thus says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}: 'Did I [not] indeed reveal {{deity_pronoun:myself|Myself}} to the house of your father when they were in Egypt, [subject] to the house of Pharaoh?

R.27: A man of God came to Eli and said to him, "This is what {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} says: 'I showed {{deity_pronoun:myself|Myself}} to your ancestors when they were in Egypt as slaves of Pharaoh.

decisions.choice: a man of God: a prophet, here unnamed
decisions.reason: "Man of God" is a title for a prophet who speaks for God (Judges 13:6; 1 Kings 13:1; 2 Kings 4:9). This one is not named; what matters is his message.

decisions.choice: did I indeed reveal myself?: a question expecting the answer yes
alternatives: I plainly revealed myself
decisions.reason: The verb is doubled for emphasis. The question is a reminder, not a request: of course God showed himself to them. The ancient Greek translation has a statement instead of a question; the sense is the same.

decisions.choice: the house of your father: the priestly family from which Eli came
alternatives: the tribe of Levi
decisions.reason: Eli's ancestor is not named. Most likely the house of Aaron, chosen as priests in Egypt and the wilderness (Exodus 4:14-16, 27; 28:1); it could also be the tribe of Levi as a whole.

decisions.choice: in Egypt, to the house of Pharaoh: under Pharaoh's rule, as his slaves
decisions.reason: "To the house of Pharaoh" means belonging to it, subject to it. The ancient Greek translation adds "slaves".

decisions.choice: the man of God's words open with a double quotation mark; the LORD's words inside them take single quotes
decisions.reason: The man of God speaks from here to the end of verse 36, and what he speaks is the LORD's message. Words the LORD quotes inside it (verses 30, 36) take double quotes again. Literal says "Thus says the LORD", Balanced "The LORD says this" and Readable "This is what the LORD says", as throughout Samuel and Kings.

decisions.choice: a statement instead of a question (Readable)
decisions.reason: Readable turns the question that expects "yes" into a statement, and says "slaves", which is what being subject to Pharaoh's house meant (Exodus 1:13-14).

records.heading: A man of God speaks against Eli's house

records.source: וּבָחֹ֣ר אֹ֠תוֹ מִכָּל־שִׁבְטֵ֨י יִשְׂרָאֵ֥ל לִי֙ לְכֹהֵ֔ן לַעֲל֣וֹת עַֽל־מִזְבְּחִ֗י לְהַקְטִ֥יר קְטֹ֛רֶת לָשֵׂ֥את אֵפ֖וֹד לְפָנָ֑י וָֽאֶתְּנָה֙ לְבֵ֣ית אָבִ֔יךָ אֶת־כָּל־אִשֵּׁ֖י בְּנֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃
records.gloss: And [did I] choose him from all [the] tribes of Israel for myself as priest, to go up on my altar, to make smoke [of] incense, to carry an ephod before me? And I gave to [the] house of your father all [the] fire offerings of [the] sons of Israel.
pieces: Out of all the tribes of Israel, did I not choose him as {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} priest, to go up to {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} altar, to offer incense, and to wear an ephod before {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}? And I gave your ancestor's family all the food offerings of the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}}.

L.28: And [did I not] choose him out of all the tribes of Israel for {{deity_pronoun:myself|Myself}} as priest, to go up on {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} altar, to burn incense, to carry an ephod before {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}? And I gave to the house of your father all the offerings by fire of the {{gender:children|sons}} of Israel.

R.28: I chose your ancestor out of all the tribes of Israel to be {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} priest. He was to offer sacrifices on {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} altar, burn incense, and wear the ephod to serve {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}. I gave your family a share of all the food offerings the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} burned on the fire.

decisions.choice: go up to the altar, burn incense, carry an ephod: the three tasks of the priest
decisions.reason: Only priests could offer on the altar (Numbers 18:7), burn incense before the LORD (Exodus 30:7-8) and carry the ephod with the Urim and Thummim, through which they sought God's answers (Exodus 28:30; 1 Samuel 14:3; 23:9).

decisions.choice: fire offerings: the offerings burned on the altar, from which the priests received their share
decisions.reason: The word names offerings made by fire. The priests and their families lived from their portion of these offerings (Leviticus 2:3; 7:34-35; Numbers 18:8-10; Deuteronomy 18:1). Eli's sons had all they needed, yet took more.

decisions.choice: did I not choose: the question of verse 27 continues
decisions.reason: The verb continues the form of the question in verse 27. God reminds Eli of everything he has given his family.

decisions.choice: a statement instead of a question (Readable)
decisions.reason: As in verse 27, Readable makes the question a statement. It says "offer sacrifices on my altar" for "go up on my altar", and "a share of" the offerings, which is what the priests were given.

decisions.choice: offerings by fire (Literal); food offerings (Balanced); food offerings burned on the fire (Readable)
decisions.reason: As in Leviticus 3.

records.source: לָ֣מָּה תִבְעֲט֗וּ בְּזִבְחִי֙ וּבְמִנְחָתִ֔י אֲשֶׁ֥ר צִוִּ֖יתִי מָע֑וֹן וַתְּכַבֵּ֤ד אֶת־בָּנֶ֨יךָ֙ מִמֶּ֔נִּי לְהַבְרִֽיאֲכֶ֗ם מֵרֵאשִׁ֛ית כָּל־מִנְחַ֥ת יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל לְעַמִּֽי׃
records.gloss: Why do you kick at my sacrifice and at my offering which I commanded [in my] dwelling, and you honor your sons more than me, by making yourselves fat from [the] best of every offering of Israel, of my people?
pieces: Why do you kick at {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} sacrifices and offerings, which I commanded for {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} dwelling? Why do you honor your sons more than {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, fattening yourselves on the best parts of every offering made by Israel, {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} people?

L.29: Why do you [all] kick at {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} sacrifice and at {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} offering, which I commanded [for {{deity_pronoun:my|My}}] dwelling, and [why do] you honor your sons more than {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, making yourselves fat on the best of every offering of Israel {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} people?

R.29: So why do you treat {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} sacrifices and offerings with such disrespect? I commanded them for {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} house. Why do you honor your sons more than you honor {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}? You make yourselves fat on the best parts of every offering {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} people Israel bring.

decisions.choice: kick at: treat with scorn, like a stubborn animal kicking
decisions.reason: The verb is used only here and in Deuteronomy 32:15, where Israel "grew fat and kicked". Here too the kicking goes with growing fat: Eli's house scorns the offerings while feeding on them.

decisions.choice: dwelling: the Hebrew word is hard to explain here
alternatives: which I commanded, with a greedy eye
decisions.reason: The Hebrew reads "which I commanded, dwelling", most likely meaning the offerings God commanded for his dwelling, the sanctuary. The ancient Greek translation read a different text, "with a greedy eye". The word returns, just as hard, in verse 32. Reviewers should check this note against the textual evidence.

decisions.choice: you kick (plural), you honor (singular): Eli shares his sons' guilt
decisions.reason: "Kick" is plural, including Eli with his sons; "honor" is singular, aimed at Eli himself. By letting his sons go on and eating with them ("making yourselves fat"), Eli has put them before God. He is called heavy in 4:18.

decisions.choice: sacrifice and offering: all the gifts brought to God
decisions.reason: The pair zevach (an animal sacrifice) and minchah (an offering or gift) together stand for every kind of offering.

decisions.choice: kick at (Literal, Balanced); treat with disrespect (Readable)
decisions.reason: Balanced keeps the vivid picture, which links this verse to Deuteronomy 32:15. Readable says what it means.

records.source: לָכֵ֗ן נְאֻם־יְהוָה֮ אֱלֹהֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵל֒ אָמ֣וֹר אָמַ֔רְתִּי בֵּֽיתְךָ֙ וּבֵ֣ית אָבִ֔יךָ יִתְהַלְּכ֥וּ לְפָנַ֖י עַד־עוֹלָ֑ם וְעַתָּ֤ה נְאֻם־יְהוָה֙ חָלִ֣ילָה לִּ֔י כִּֽי־מְכַבְּדַ֥י אֲכַבֵּ֖ד וּבֹזַ֥י יֵקָֽלּוּ׃
records.gloss: Therefore declaration of Yahweh, God of Israel: indeed I said, your house and [the] house of your father will walk before me until forever; but now declaration of Yahweh: far be it from me, for those honoring me I will honor, and those despising me will be lightly esteemed.
pieces: Therefore {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, the God of Israel, declares: I did promise that your family and your ancestor's family would walk before {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} forever. But now {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} declares: That will never be! For I will honor those who honor {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, and those who despise {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} will be treated as nothing.

L.30: Therefore, declares {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, the God of Israel, I did indeed say, "Your house and the house of your father will walk before {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} forever"; but now, declares {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, far be it from {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}! For those who honor {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} I will honor, and those who despise {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} will be lightly esteemed.

R.30: So this is what {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, the God of Israel, says: I promised that your family would serve before {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} as priests forever. But now {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} says: I will never let that happen! I will honor people who honor {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}. But people who despise {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} will be treated as worthless.

decisions.choice: walk before me: live and serve in my presence
decisions.reason: To walk before God is to live in his sight and serve him. Here it means serving as priests at his sanctuary.

decisions.choice: I did say ... but now far be it from me: a promise withdrawn
decisions.reason: God had promised the priesthood to Aaron's line forever (Exodus 29:9; compare Numbers 25:13). That promise still stands for the priesthood, but this branch of the family loses it because it has despised him (verse 35; 1 Kings 2:27).

decisions.choice: far be it from me: an emphatic refusal
decisions.reason: The phrase rejects something as unthinkable. God will not keep honoring a house that dishonors him.

decisions.choice: honor, lightly esteemed: heavy and light
decisions.reason: The verb "honor" comes from the word for "heavy", giving weight; "lightly esteemed" is from the word for "light". Those who give God weight he will give weight; those who make light of him will count for nothing.

decisions.choice: I did promise that ... (Balanced, Readable)
decisions.reason: Literal quotes God's earlier words. Balanced and Readable report them as a promise, which they were, and so need no further quotation marks. "Declares the LORD" follows the wording used throughout Samuel and Kings.

decisions.choice: serve before me as priests (Readable)
decisions.reason: Readable says what walking before God meant for Eli's family, and folds "the house of your father" into "your family".

records.source: הִנֵּה֙ יָמִ֣ים בָּאִ֔ים וְגָֽדַעְתִּי֙ אֶת־זְרֹ֣עֲךָ֔ וְאֶת־זְרֹ֖עַ בֵּ֣ית אָבִ֑יךָ מִֽהְי֥וֹת זָקֵ֖ן בְּבֵיתֶֽךָ׃
records.gloss: Look, days [are] coming, and I will cut off your arm and [the] arm of [the] house of your father, from being an old man in your house.
pieces: The time is coming when I will break your strength and the strength of your ancestor's family, so that no one in your family will live to old age.

L.31: Look, days are coming when I will cut off your arm and the arm of the house of your father, so that there will not be an old man in your house.

R.31: A time is coming when I will break the strength of your family. No one in your family will live to be old.

decisions.choice: arm: strength
decisions.reason: The arm stands for a person's strength and power. To cut off the arm is to break the family's strength.

decisions.choice: no old man in your house: all will die before they grow old
decisions.reason: The men of Eli's family will die young. The slaughter of the priests of Nob, Eli's descendants, is the first great fulfillment (22:16-19).

decisions.choice: strength (Balanced, Readable)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps "arm". Balanced and Readable give its sense. "Look" stands for the word often rendered "behold"; Balanced and Readable leave it out and let "the time is coming" carry the stress.

records.source: וְהִבַּטְתָּ֙ צַ֣ר מָע֔וֹן בְּכֹ֥ל אֲשֶׁר־יֵיטִ֖יב אֶת־יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל וְלֹֽא־יִהְיֶ֥ה זָקֵ֛ן בְּבֵיתְךָ֖ כָּל־הַיָּמִֽים׃
records.gloss: And you will look on distress of dwelling in all that he will do good to Israel; and not will be an old man in your house all the days.
pieces: In {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} dwelling you will see distress, even while Israel is given every good thing, and no one in your family will ever live to old age.

L.32: And you will look on [the] distress of [{{deity_pronoun:my|My}}] dwelling, in all the good that will be done for Israel; and there will not be an old man in your house all the days.

R.32: You will see trouble come on {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} house, even while good things are done for the rest of Israel. And no one in your family will ever grow old.

decisions.choice: you will see distress in my dwelling: the meaning is uncertain
alternatives: you will look on a rival in my dwelling
decisions.reason: The Hebrew is hard. It reads "distress of dwelling", most likely trouble at God's dwelling, the sanctuary at Shiloh: the ark would be captured and Shiloh ruined (4:10-22; Jeremiah 7:12-14; Psalm 78:60-61). The first word can also mean "rival", giving "you will look on a rival in my dwelling", another priest in the place of Eli's house. The ancient Greek translation and a Dead Sea Scroll lack most of this verse. Reviewers should check this note against the textual evidence.

decisions.choice: in all the good that will be done for Israel: while things go well for Israel
decisions.reason: The verb is "he will do good", with no named subject; it is God who does good to Israel. Eli's house suffers even while Israel as a whole is blessed.

decisions.choice: you: Eli's house through the years
decisions.reason: "You" is Eli, standing for his family; most of what is foretold came after his death.

decisions.choice: my dwelling (Literal in brackets, Balanced, Readable)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew has only "dwelling". All three levels supply "my", since God is speaking of his own sanctuary, as in verse 29.

records.source: וְאִ֗ישׁ לֹֽא־אַכְרִ֤ית לְךָ֙ מֵעִ֣ם מִזְבְּחִ֔י לְכַלּ֥וֹת אֶת־עֵינֶ֖יךָ וְלַאֲדִ֣יב אֶת־נַפְשֶׁ֑ךָ וְכָל־מַרְבִּ֥ית בֵּיתְךָ֖ יָמ֥וּתוּ אֲנָשִֽׁים׃
records.gloss: And a man not I will cut off of yours from with my altar, to make fail your eyes and to grieve your soul; and all [the] increase of your house will die [as] men.
pieces: Yet one of your descendants I will not cut off from serving at {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} altar, so that your eyes will fail with weeping and your heart will grieve. All the rest of your descendants will die in the prime of life.

L.33: Yet one man of yours I will not cut off from {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} altar, to make your eyes fail and to grieve your soul; and all the increase of your house will die [as] men.

R.33: I will let one man from your family go on serving at {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} altar. But his life will bring you tears and sorrow. All the rest of your family will die before they grow old.

decisions.choice: one man I will not cut off: a single survivor left to serve
alternatives: any man of yours whom I do not cut off
decisions.reason: One of Eli's line will be spared to go on serving at the altar. This came true in Abiathar, who alone escaped the slaughter at Nob (22:20-23) and was later removed from the priesthood by Solomon (1 Kings 2:26-27).

decisions.choice: to make your eyes fail and to grieve your soul: to bring weeping and grief
decisions.reason: Eyes "fail" from weeping until they can weep no more. Even the survivor's life will be a sorrow to Eli's house.

decisions.choice: will die as men: in the prime of life
alternatives: will die by the sword of men
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says they will die "as men", grown men, not old men (verse 31). The ancient Greek translation and a Dead Sea Scroll read "by the sword of men". Reviewers should check this note against the textual evidence.

decisions.choice: the rest of your descendants (Balanced); the rest of your family (Readable)
decisions.reason: "The increase of your house" means its offspring. Balanced and Readable add "the rest" to set them apart from the one survivor.

records.source: וְזֶה־לְּךָ֣ הָא֗וֹת אֲשֶׁ֤ר יָבֹא֙ אֶל־שְׁנֵ֣י בָנֶ֔יךָ אֶל־חָפְנִ֖י וּפִֽינְחָ֑ס בְּי֥וֹם אֶחָ֖ד יָמ֥וּתוּ שְׁנֵיהֶֽם׃
records.gloss: And this to you [is] the sign which will come to [the] two of your sons, to Hophni and Phinehas: on day one will die both of them.
pieces: What happens to your two sons, Hophni and Phinehas, will be the sign to you: both of them will die on the same day.

L.34: And this [will be] the sign to you, which will come on your two sons, on Hophni and Phinehas: on one day the two of them will die.

R.34: This is how you will know that what I say will come true: your two sons, Hophni and Phinehas, will both die on the same day.

decisions.choice: the sign: a near event that proves the longer word true
decisions.reason: Eli will live to hear of his sons' deaths, and that will show that the rest of the message will also come true. Both die in one day in battle with the Philistines (4:11, 17).

decisions.choice: This is how you will know that what I say will come true (Readable)
decisions.reason: Readable explains what the sign is for.

records.source: וַהֲקִימֹתִ֥י לִי֙ כֹּהֵ֣ן נֶאֱמָ֔ן כַּאֲשֶׁ֛ר בִּלְבָבִ֥י וּבְנַפְשִׁ֖י יַעֲשֶׂ֑ה וּבָנִ֤יתִי לוֹ֙ בַּ֣יִת נֶאֱמָ֔ן וְהִתְהַלֵּ֥ךְלִפְנֵֽי־מְשִׁיחִ֖י כָּל־הַיָּמִֽים׃
records.gloss: And I will raise up for myself a priest faithful; according to what [is] in my heart and in my soul he will do; and I will build for him a house sure, and he will walk before my anointed all the days.
pieces: I will raise up for {{deity_pronoun:myself|Myself}} a faithful priest, who will do what is in {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} heart and mind. I will build him a lasting house, and he will walk before {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} anointed for all time.

L.35: And I will raise up for {{deity_pronoun:myself|Myself}} a faithful priest; he will do according to what [is] in {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} heart and in {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} soul. And I will build for him a sure house, and he will walk before {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} anointed all the days.

R.35: I will choose a priest for {{deity_pronoun:myself|Myself}} who will be faithful to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}. He will do everything I want him to do. I will give him a family line that will last, and he will always serve the king I have anointed.

decisions.choice: a faithful priest: who is meant
alternatives: Samuel
Zadok
decisions.reason: In the story that follows, Samuel fills this role first: the LORD is with him, all Israel knows he is faithful (3:19-20), and he offers sacrifices for the people (7:9). But a priest with a lasting house who serves before the king points most fully to Zadok, who replaced Abiathar of Eli's line under Solomon; 1 Kings 2:27 and 2:35 say this fulfilled the word spoken at Shiloh.

decisions.choice: faithful priest, sure house: the same word twice
decisions.reason: The word ne'eman means faithful, firm, reliable. The priest will be faithful, and so God will make his house firm and lasting. God makes the same promise of a sure house to David (2 Samuel 7:16; compare 1 Samuel 25:28).

decisions.choice: my anointed: the king God will appoint
decisions.reason: As in Hannah's song (verse 10), the prophecy looks ahead to a king Israel does not yet have. The priest will serve in the presence of the LORD's anointed king.

decisions.choice: in my heart and in my soul: in my mind and my will
decisions.reason: Heart and soul together mean what God thinks and desires. The faithful priest will act as God wants.

decisions.choice: a sure house (Literal); a lasting house (Balanced); a family line that will last (Readable)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps "sure", the same word as "faithful". Balanced says "lasting". Readable says what "house" means here: a line of descendants.

decisions.choice: the king I have anointed (Readable)
decisions.reason: As in verse 10, Readable says who "my anointed" is.

records.gloss: And it will be, everyone who is left in your house will come to bow down to him for a payment of silver and a loaf of bread, and say, attach me, please, to one of the priesthoods, to eat a piece of bread.
pieces: Then everyone left in your family will come and bow down to him for a little silver and a loaf of bread, and say, "Please put me in one of the priestly posts so that I can have a scrap of bread to eat."'"

L.36: And it will be [that] everyone who is left in your house will come to bow down to him for a payment of silver and a loaf of bread, and will say, "Please attach me to one of the priestly offices, that I may eat a piece of bread."'"

R.36: Anyone left in your family will come and bow down to him. They will beg for a little money and a piece of bread. They will say, "Please give me some kind of priestly job, so that I will have something to eat."'"

decisions.choice: a payment of silver: a small coin or wage
decisions.reason: The noun is found only here. It seems to mean a small payment, a coin or a day's pay.

decisions.choice: the priestly offices: duties at the sanctuary that came with a share of the offerings
decisions.reason: Priests lived from their part of what was offered (Deuteronomy 18:1-8). A lesser post would still give food. Compare the priests of the high places in 2 Kings 23:9, who ate bread among their brothers but did not serve at the altar.

decisions.choice: a piece of bread: the house that took by force will beg
decisions.reason: Eli's sons seized the best meat from the worshipers (verses 13-16). Their descendants will beg for a scrap of bread.

decisions.choice: the quotation marks close here: the double quote of the beggar's words, the single quote of the LORD's words, and the double quote of the man of God's speech
decisions.reason: The man of God's message, which began in verse 27, ends with this verse.
